tarot.cyberneticenhancements.death.descr:
Death is the card of becoming.

It signifies an imminent and difficult transition – the conclusion of one phase of life and the beginning of another.

Inevitably, something gets lost during the transformation, but something else will rise and take its place.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.judgement.d:
Judgement is the card of renewal.

The angel blowing into the horn heralds resurrection and liberation.

This card foretells an important change that will result in healing or fulfillment. It is also a symbol of self-worth.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.justice.des:
Justice is the card of conflict resolution.

It proclaims the need for order, to see through lies and deceit, and a return to the natural state of affairs.

Justice implies a just sentence, but also due process.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.king_of_cup:
A King of Cups is a creative and emotionally-driven person.

They are strong individuals, who realize the importance of feelings. Intuition helps them navigate their lives.

When fate is in their favor, compassion guides their actions. When they're at odds with fate, it'd be unwise to trust them.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.king_of_pen:
The King of Pentacles is imperious.

They represent enterprise, pragmatism, but also attachment.

From such a person one can expect coldness or attachment to material possessions; they are likely to turn your world upside down sooner or later.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.king_of_swo:
Two things matter above all else for a King of Swords: logic and conviction.

They represent a person with a precise moral compass, who is known for their caring demeanor.

However, enemies beware - the King of Swords is a ruthless opponent, who will not rest until you are punished and left to be torn apart by hounds of fate.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.king_of_wan:
The master of planning and unorthodox ideas.

An individual who brings people together and radiates inspiration to those they consider friends.

However, their enemies will soon find they are an impulsive, devastating force of nature, capable of breaking oaths and crossing any line, just to see their goals achieved.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.knight_of_c:
The Knight of Cups is a seeker with stars in their eyes and a burning fire in their chest.

They thrive on taking action, driven not by logic but by longing. This is a card of newfound vision and ideas that stir the soul.

When the world shatters their heart, the reckoning may echo violently.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.knight_of_p:
When a line is crossed, the Knight of Pentacles is who you want standing at your side.

This card represents those who protect what is theirs. The Knight's stubborn nature does not serve the pursuit of new glory or fame, but the safeguarding of legacy.

It also symbolizes the preservation of songs written in one's own blood.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.knight_of_s:
The Knight of Swords is a harbinger of dramatic change.

It signifies leaving the comfort of the known world for new ventures without looking back, no matter the risk. It represents one who values honesty and clarity above all else.

Their forthright nature can sometimes sting; yet, this aversion to deceit should be considered a gift for friend and foe alike.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.knight_of_w:
The Knight of Wands does not wait for permission. The presence of obstacles only proves they're on the right path.

Beneath an outward swagger lies a genuine hunger for greatness, and fear takes a back seat when adventure calls.

They leap before looking, but even when they fall they never stop moving forward.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.page_of_cup:
The Page of Cups drifts through the world with open eyes and an open heart.

To some, they appear naive; to others, virtuous. This card represents the youthfulness of one's spirit, their hopes, instincts and ideals.

Their dreams today will reshape their tomorrow, assuming they survive the arrows of fate.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.page_of_pen:
For the Page of Pentacles, every horizon is the gateway to a new beginning.

They inevitably make mistakes and burn bridges, but never lose faith that they are working toward something better.

Drawing this card signals a moment when fear of the future dissipates, revealing a promising plan.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.page_of_swo:
The Page of Swords never drops their guard.

Curious and calculating, their inquisitive and innovative nature defines their trajectory and the fortunes of those around them.

This card signifies an approaching beginning that requires careful consideration of all pathways and outcomes. When preparing for anything, one's awareness becomes their armor.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.page_of_wan:
The Page of Wands lives for sparks of inspiration and the promise of new opportunities.

Growth is the only constant; change - the only rule.

Their journey is messy, imperfect, but always high-spirited. In the craters of ruin they sow all they can, knowing whatever sprouts may be the beginning of something revolutionary.

Cannot place here; check building permissions
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.placement.w: Aim at a clear 2 x 3 wall
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.queen_of_cu:
The Queen of Cups is a wellspring of calm.

She listens more than she speaks, understands more than she reveals, and sees what others bury deep.

In her presence, broken spirits can learn to hope again.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.queen_of_pe:
The Queen of Pentacles lives boldly and wears luxury like a suit of armor.

She opens her doors without fear, offering comfort, generosity and connection.

She knows what it means to lose oneself and find another standing in their place. This card represents a return to something real.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.queen_of_sw:
The Queen of Swords rules with her razor wit and a tongue that cuts deeper than folded steel.

She seeks truth in all things and will not tolerate deceit. This is a card of clear-eyed independence, wisdom, intellect, and an ability to see through illusions.

She walks alone, not because she must, but because few can keep her pace and embrace life without the protection of a mask.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.queen_of_wa:
The Queen of Wands stands firm when others waver and flee. She is both bulwark and spearhead.

Her courage isn't loud, but it echoes with a spirit of independence that endures long after the noise fades.

Drawing this card marks a moment when one must protect what matters most.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.reward.head: +%s chrome headroom
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.reward_help: Each distinct card grants two bonuses. No chrome cost; duplicates do not stack.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.strength.de:
Strength is the card of resilience.

It is associated with determination, bravery and internal struggle. One must have dedication in order to overcome obstacles and reach one's goal.

Strength is about physical prowess and spiritual fortitude – the power that must be unleashed to achieve the impossible.
Temperance is the card of balance.

It may symbolize self-restraint or the gradual shift toward a more mature state of equilibrium.

Temperance is associated with being in control of oneself as well as the desire to achieve inner peace.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_chariot:
The Chariot is always charging ahead despite being pulled by its steeds in opposite directions.

The rider who steers it constantly reins in the light and dark sides of the soul with the help of Reason.

To ride in The Chariot is to experience highs and lows – ups and downs.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_devil.d:
The Devil is addiction, craving and passion.

He brings fame and fortune, but at the price of losing oneself to a world of material distractions.

The Devil lures unsuspecting souls into traps, but always grants them a choice. One can try their luck and take him up on his offer, but one should always know when to call quits.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_emperor:
The Emperor represents patriarchal control and is pleased with the authority and power he possesses to shape the future.

The Emperor makes the rules and enforces them for the common good.

But prestige has its dark sides – the Emperor is dominating and ruthless and will climb over a mountain of bodies to achieve his aim.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_empress:
The empress is a card of femininity and motherhood.

She is authoritative, knows what she wants, and exhibits refinement and sensuousness.

The Empress symbolizes creativity and growth, and instructs us not to dismiss our unconscious impulses, but to trust our intuition.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_fool.de:
The Fool is everyone - including you and me.

Each step he takes on his journey feels like stepping into a brave new world.

Ultimately, the journey will change him. But as the card shows, he's a trustworthy lad whose tireless hope drives him toward his goal.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_hanged_:
The Hanged Man is the card of sacrifice.

It says that a price must be paid in order to achieve enlightenment.

The Hanged Man's forsakenness opens the path for rebirth into a new life, though this path is wrought with pain suspended in time and ultimately ends in death.
The Hermit is a card of self-imposed isolation.

It represents an escape from the hustle and bustle of the city, a turning away from constant newness toward Ye Olde ways.

For the hermit, solitude is the road to the sublime – a road that is taken not with great bounds and strides, but with small, concentrated steps.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_hieroph:
The Hierophant symbolizes a respect for tradition.

It represents one who tries to maintain the established order, even though their very character is shaped by it.

The Hierophant places his faith in institutions – for the alternative is pure chaos. Only by placing his faith in order can he draw strength.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_high_pr:
The High Priestess is a card of mystery.

It shows how all our secrets hang by a delicate thread and the struggle between common sense and intuition.

The High Priestess symbolizes the cold, calm waters as well as the mysteries hidden in their depths.
The Lovers is the card of dichotomies.

It points to the contradictions that clash within each of us and of the challenge of striking a balance between extremes.

The Lovers is also the card of dilemmas, like The Fool who stands at the crossroads, unable to make his choice.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_magicia:
The Magician is the card of self-confidence and adapting to situations through intellect and sheer will.

The Magician is a schemer who always has one last trick up his sleeve, who despite everything manages to stay afloat and remain in control of his own destiny.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_moon.de:
The Moon reminds us that reality is not always what it seems at first glance.

In a world of appearances and illusions, the best course is often charted by one's own intuition.

The Moon is also the card of dreams, desires, and of course, sleep – Death's nightly ritual.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_star.de:
The Star is the card of hope.

In the darkest of nights there is a light that shines the path to home.

The Star is inspiration, motivation and gives us strength to move forward.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_sun.des:
The Sun symbolizes success. It is a card of freedom, renewal and a bright future that lies ahead.

The Sun also represents truth, for its light will always pull back the curtain of shadow that hides the world's secrets.

It is also represents greatness and splendor.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_tower.d:
The Tower is an omen of radical change, chaos and destruction.

The lightning striking The Tower signifies a return to the old order that lies buried under the ruins, and a new order that will rise from it.

It is a symbol of tragedy, apocalypse, and self-destruction.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.the_world.d:
The World lies at the end of The Fool's long and winding journey.

Wiser and more world-weary than he started out, the Fool faces a moment of reckoning. Some of us accept where our journey has led us to, while others embark on a new challenge.

One thing in this World is certain – you can't have it all.
tarot.cyberneticenhancements.wheel_of_fo:
The Wheel of Fortune means that change is coming.

One's destiny could turn out for the better or the worse, yet it also bears the promise of new possibilities.

The Wheel reminds us that nobody remains at the top forever, but also that not every situation is hopeless.

wiki.cyberneticenhancements.encounter.sh: Nobody (levels 1-19): easy money. Four of them come, with a toll of %s%% of your balance (%s to %s), only %s seconds to answer, and your chrome impresses them half as much. A shakedown is the street's favourite thing to do to a nobody, so they happen more often.

Street names (levels 20-49): the plain version, three of them, %s%% of your balance (%s to %s) and %s seconds. From level 20 you can also say your name instead of paying, and the higher your level, the likelier they know it.
Known names (levels 50-79): only two come, the toll is %s%% (%s to %s) and you get %s seconds. They are better armed, but reputation adds %s%% to the chance that a refusal is taken seriously.

Feared names (levels 80-100): two of them, much tougher, with a toll of only %s%% (%s to %s) and %s seconds to decide. Most of the time they do not come to take at all: they come with tribute, %s to %s eurodollars. Take it for the money, or turn it down for the respect.
Saying your name chance: %s%% at level 20, %s%% at level 50 and %s%% at level 100. Backing a gang down, or turning down their tribute, earns %s Street Cred. Failing makes them attack.
The gang appears as holograms ten to sixteen blocks away and walks up to you.
The toll is a share of your eurodollar balance, kept within a range that depends on your Street Cred.
You have a limited time to answer, longer the bigger your name. Say nothing and the gang attacks.
Once hostile, the gang hunts only you, and gives up if you get far away or they have been around for eight minutes.
Defeating them does not bring MaxTec.
Pay: the gang takes the toll and leaves as holograms. If you cannot afford it, they take offence and attack.
Refuse: a bluff. Each implant you have installed adds a chance that the gang backs down, and a name adds more. If it fails, they attack.
Fight: striking any of them also ends the negotiation and turns the whole gang on you.

A street gang closes in on you and demands a toll. Who comes, what they ask and how they treat you depends on your Street Cred. They talk first and only fight once you turn them down or the time runs out.

Shakedowns follow the same timing as other street encounters, but never happen on Peaceful difficulty or to players with less than 50 eurodollars. Operators can trigger one with /cyberneticenhancements encounter trigger shakedown.

Implants still have to be installed at a Ripper Station. The doctor only sells them.
A mobile ripperdoc is never a contact: there is no trust, no discount, no renaming and no entry in your contacts archive. Prices are fixed and nothing is locked behind trust.
Killing one is allowed and does not bring MaxTec down on you.

Now and then a street ripperdoc picks you out and heads your way. They sell real chrome from a street stock of tiers one to three, plus clinic supplies, and offer two services you will not find at a permanent contact.

Encounters happen in the overworld, under open sky, roughly every twenty to forty minutes. Operators can trigger one with /cyberneticenhancements encounter trigger ripperdoc, and the gamerule cyberneticStreetEncounters turns them off.

Successful business and completed contracts build a gradual relationship. The contact screen shows your trust percentage and next unlock.
Trust is stored per player and per contact UUID. Rapport with one contact does not unlock another.
Attacking a contact, wasting a requested meetup, or repeatedly attempting unaffordable purchases can lower trust.
Accumulated annoyance can temporarily increase prices or make the contact refuse service.
Heat can cause a roughly two-minute price surcharge or four-minute refusal window. Let it expire before returning.
On your first login, the nearest Night City is marked on your HUD compass to help you meet NPCs. Entering that city disables its marker once, without deleting it. Open Neural Archive > Compass > Markers and choose Cities to show it again, rename it or change its color. The location, visit status and visibility are saved for your player across deaths and reconnects.

The Contacts tab records every NPC you have actually interacted with. Each NPC card shows the head render, name, type, trust state and live or last known location. Online players also appear as Player contacts, with their skin, voice availability and Pin, Block and Call controls. Use the type filter or search to find them. Pinned and blocked player contacts remain listed offline. Blocking prevents calls in either direction; use Unblock on their card to undo it.

Search contacts by name or NPC type, then use Type: All types to select an archetype. All, Pinned, Deceased and Hidden filters work together with search and type selection. Hidden contacts appear only under Hidden.
Each card supports Pin or Unpin plus Hide or Unhide. These flags are stored per player, so one player's organization does not change another player's archive.

Press K during gameplay for quick-call contacts with faces and colored names. Pinned contacts appear first. Use Alt+1 through Alt+3 to call a visible contact, Alt+4 for the next page and Alt+5 to close. Calls use the same compact HUD while you keep moving and playing: Alt+1 through Alt+5 answer, Alt+0 hangs up. All controls can be rebound in Minecraft Controls.

Calls ring for varying lengths of time. Annoyed contacts may decline or ignore them, and occupied lines are busy. Replies vary with time, weather and trust. Ask contract contacts about available jobs, hear the objective and reward, then accept on the call. Ask about your current job's progress, instructions or destination. Ready objectives without a physical handover can be reported over a call or from the Quests tab. Recovery supplies, extraction shards and cyberpsycho dossiers must be handed to the quest giver in person. Money, trust and XP are immediate; item rewards reach your Dropoff Point within one Minecraft day. In-person turn-ins give items immediately. Confirmed deaths remain in Contacts with a red Deceased status and disabled calls, including after server restarts. Unloaded contacts are not treated as dead. Connected NPCs hold a phone in the world. Look at your contact within interaction range to switch to in-person dialogue.

Contacts can call you. Answer with Alt+1 or decline with Alt+2; unanswered calls stop after 30 seconds. Connected NPCs hang up after 10 seconds without a conversation reply, with no trust or quest penalty. An issuer may check on a contract after two hours of online play time. Trusted contacts may occasionally ask for a small contribution, which you must explicitly approve; declining a money request costs nothing. Automatic calls have a 30-minute overall cooldown and a two-hour repeat cooldown per contract, money request or urgent issuer; these survive reconnects and respawns. Hidden contacts do not make routine calls; missing quest evidence can still trigger an angry call.

Contract issuers can occasionally call with a specific urgent job when you have no active contract from them. Answer to review the objective and boosted payout. Accepting through that offer adds 25% money and one extra trust to its completion rewards. Explicitly refusing the job costs one trust and withdraws that offer; missing or declining the ringing call costs nothing. Urgent contracts are labeled in the quest log and keep their bonus through saving and reconnects. Urgency does not add a completion deadline.
Five archetypes are live: [[npc_fixer|Fixer]], [[npc_ripperdoc|Ripperdoc]], [[npc_techie|Techie]], [[npc_netrunner|Netrunner]] and [[npc_merc|Merc]]. Each has its own stock, services and dialogue.
Techies, Netrunners and Mercs issue [[quest_guide_overview|contracts]], including Cyberpsycho Sightings. Fixers and Netrunners offer cache intel.
NPC names and categories come from config/cyberneticenhancements-npc-identities.properties.
The file separates male_names, female_names and generic_names. The chosen category also selects the texture folder under assets/cyberneticenhancements/textures/entity/npc/<category>/.
Skins are rendered on the player model with second-layer parts enabled, so hats, jackets and similar overlay pixels show if the texture provides them.
NPCs retain their identity, home and per-player relationships.

Each player keeps separate trust and interaction flags with the same NPC. Blue names mean friendly; hurting a contact turns their name yellow for you for five minutes. They turn red and defend themselves below 25% health. An amber bar below their health shows the remaining aggression cooldown and refills when you hit them again. After five seconds without another attack, or when you leave the immediate area, they stop fighting and return to yellow. Anger fades after five minutes; temporary refusals last at most four minutes after the last provocation. Trust can be earned back. Surviving contacts start healing after 20 seconds without damage, recovering one health point every five seconds. Red names mean aggressive enemies, including cyberpsychos and MaxTec. Name colors indicate behavior and cannot be customized. Killing a contact deploys a four-officer MaxTec squad against the killer, with dedicated skins and working combat cyberware. Sandevistan slows cyberpsychos and MaxTec even when they are idle or targeting someone else. Player-credited kills drop XP: 2 for ordinary NPCs, 25 per MaxTec officer, and 50/75/100 for tier 1/2/3 cyberpsychos. Combat XP follows vanilla mob-loot rules.
NPCs use player-style skins and rendering, can be called through the archive, and are meant to stay relevant beyond a single screen click.
Shared NPC rules, contact tracking and identity behavior across the whole NPC layer.

Each lifepath has its own entry: [[origin_nomad|Nomad]], [[origin_street_kid|Street Kid]] and [[origin_corpo|Corpo]]. Every entry lists the players who chose it, for example the [[origin_corpo#players|Corpo players]].
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.origin.playe: Every player who has chosen this lifepath, in alphabetical order.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.origin.roste: Nobody has chosen this lifepath yet.

Money range includes material compensation; the exact amount depends on the requested item and quantity.
In-person turn-ins give items immediately. Remote turn-ins pay money, trust and XP immediately; items arrive at your [[station_dropoff|Dropoff Point]] within one Minecraft day.

One separate bonus roll awards a missing schematic, or a fallback part if all eligible designs are learned. The pool updates as designs are learned. Tier 3 Cyberpsycho jobs roll for a restricted core first; a core replaces the schematic/part bonus.
Failed or abandoned contracts pay no completion rewards. Abandonment costs at least 2 trust, or the contract's trust reward +2 if higher. A failed breach has no second attempt.
Bonus part: %s chance of 1 x %s (all eligible schematics learned).
One fallback part replaces the schematic when all eligible designs are learned.
Money, trust, XP and listed supplies are guaranteed on successful turn-in. Amounts and discovery chances use this server's economy settings.
Available contracts vary with the contact's type, your trust, daily offers and available target sites.
One active contract per contact, with no total limit. Boards refresh each Minecraft day. Use the compass to follow the active objective.
Reach the marked cache and complete its breach puzzle. Failure ends the contract and triggers an angry call from the issuer; prepare before starting.

The Techie's investigation variant: take three separated readings around the geological prospect by crouching with empty hands. Completion reveals a chromium deposit and pays four Chromium Alloy Ingots instead of the normal investigation supply.

Defeat the cyberpsycho, loot the dossier and return it to the issuer. Losing it for 10 seconds triggers an angry call: confirm you still own it in external storage, or the quest fails when you admit the loss, decline or miss the call. Dossiers are never replaced.

Carry the Courier Package to the marked Iron Quest Crate. Lost packages are not restored automatically: call the issuer for another. Replacements reduce completion rewards and bonus chances to 50%; whole-number rewards round down. Earlier copies become invalid.
Travel to the marked encounter and defeat the assigned hostile targets. Required kills increase with tier.

Recover the extraction shard, then return it to the issuer. If it goes missing for 10 seconds, the issuer calls angrily. Admit the loss, decline or miss the call and the quest fails. Say you still have it to keep the quest open while it is in external storage. Lost shards are never replaced.
Take three separated bearings by crouching with empty hands in the survey area. Triangulate the signal, then reach its source.
Gather the requested material and quantity from your inventory, then hand it over. The payout includes material compensation.
%s eligible unlearned designs; %s per design. Pool updates as you learn schematics.
Stars are a guide to travel, preparation and combat demands, not a success probability. Higher contract tiers increase difficulty; terrain and equipment also matter.
No guaranteed supply item at this tier.
Also reveals the surveyed chromium deposit marker on successful completion.
Trust level 0 offers tier 1. Level 1 unlocks tier 2; level 3 unlocks tier 3. Each available tier is equally likely when an offer is generated.
Hold the required item and right-click the issuing NPC to hand it over without opening dialogue. Keep the full requested quantity in your inventory. Dialogue turn-in is also available.
Once ready, turn in through the Quests tab, a call or the issuing NPC.
Nothing needs to be carried back. Walk up to the issuing NPC and tell them in person, through dialogue, to complete the quest.
Urgent contracts pay 25% more money (rounded up) and +1 extra trust. Tier summaries show normal payouts.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.quests.curre: Seven contract types are implemented: Delivery, Extraction, Investigation, Breach, Elimination, Recovery and Cyberpsycho Sighting. The available mix depends on the issuing contact.

Completed jobs pay eurodollars, trust and 15-120 XP points based on type and tier, may include supplies, and can award missing fabrication schematics or parts. Recovery payments include compensation for the requested materials. Bundled ordinary contracts discover designs up to tier four; tier-three Cyberpsycho Sightings can reach tier-five designs and restricted cores. XP is paid once at turn-in, including by call or the Quests tab; failed, abandoned and cancelled jobs give none. Server datapacks control money, trust and discovery chances.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.quests.cyber: Cyberpsycho Sightings are high-risk jobs from Techies, Netrunners and Mercs. The compass shows a 48-block search area. Find the named opponent, whose red name warns that they are aggressive. Expect heavy armor, high health and one of five working cyberware loadouts: mantis blades, thermal blades, shock blades, projectile launcher or gorilla arms. Blade lunges and launcher shots have windups; missiles do not damage terrain. Kill the subject, loot their named information shard and hand it to the issuer in person. The dossier is required for payment and identifies the subject and their cyberware. These jobs have the highest standard money payouts and enhanced trust rewards. There is a 25% chance of recovering a damaged implant matching the enemy's loadout. Your encounter persists across reloads, and lost dossiers trigger an angry call after 10 seconds missing; confirm external storage to keep the quest, or it fails.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.quests.plann: The Quests tab separates Active, Completed, Abandoned, Failed and Cancelled contracts, and tracks objectives, destinations and ready turn-ins. Delivery deposits a package in an Iron Quest Crate; Extraction retrieves a shard from the same metal container; Investigation triangulates a hidden source from three separated, stationary scans and then breaches its secured cache; Breach completes a secured cache in one committed attempt; failure costs trust and successes disappear after payout; Elimination defeats targets; Recovery supplies requested items; Cyberpsycho Sighting locates and defeats a named, heavily augmented opponent, then returns their information shard in person. Confirmed issuer deaths, unavailable dimensions and invalid destinations cancel contracts without trust loss or rewards. Missing containers and unstarted caches are restored only where safe. A blocked site or missing encounter cancels after 30 seconds of nearby checks; unloaded sites and time spent away do not count. Cancelled history explains the reason. Started breaches still have one attempt and their normal failure penalty.

You can hold one active contract per issuing contact, with no total limit. Extraction shards, recovery supplies and cyberpsycho dossiers must be handed to the issuer in person. Other ready objectives can be reported through the Quests tab, a call or the issuer. Remote item rewards go to your Dropoff Point within one Minecraft day; in-person handovers give items immediately.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.quests.reser: Contract boards and the quest log are live for Techie, Netrunner and Merc contacts.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.recycle.cond: Recovery bands: at least %s%% integrity is good; %s%% to below that is worn; below %s%% is heavily damaged.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.recycle.exam: The illustrated batch is a full-integrity example. Insert your actual item into the Recycler to see its exact condition-dependent recovery.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.recycle.no_r: Each recycling cycle destroys one input and commits the entire previewed batch. Stored chips and modules are destroyed with their host; upgrades are not refunded and no schematic is learned.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.recycle.unav: This server has no recycling recipe for this implant.
Install a functional Sandevistan in your operating-system slot at a [[station_ripper|Ripper Station]]. Press the operating-system ability key (V by default) to engage or disengage. Manual cancellation keeps the activation cost and recovery period.

Nearby hostile mobs move, think, attack and wind up more slowly. Fully recovered melee strikes can connect at your accelerated attack rate against affected mobs. Incoming arrows, tridents and supported thrown projectiles advance physically in smaller steps and still collide and inflict damage. Your own and other accelerated users' shots retain their speed.

Militech Experimental Sandevistan is a legendary-cache prototype inspired by David Martinez. It can also be fabricated after learning its design and obtaining the restricted parts. It offers intense acceleration with high strain and wear; no flight, teleportation, automatic critical hits or damage immunity.

Condition reduces efficiency and active duration. Every engagement causes wear and adds existing [[cyberpsychosis|neurological instability]]. Repeated activations within the recovery window add further strain. Repair the implant at a [[station_tech|Repair Station]]; a broken device cannot activate.

Dynalar is forgiving; Zetatech rewards airborne movement; Falcon sustains aggressive combat; Warp Dancer favors precision; Apogee combines strong acceleration with bounded kill rewards. At most six distinct hostile takedowns reward Falcon or Apogee, and active time cannot exceed 150% of its initial duration.

Time dilation is local. Other players keep normal controls; accelerated users cannot freeze one another. Overlapping fields use the strongest effect. World time, redstone and distant encounters continue normally. Bosses and encounter-specific projectiles are exempt.
Afterimages, edge pulses, FOV and sound volume have separate client presentation settings. Disabling them does not weaken the ability. Server balance and upgrade datapacks control gameplay.

Overload is a predictable danger of repeated unsafe use or severe damage, not a random first-use failure. It ends acceleration, damages the implant, inflicts a short physical aftershock and doubles recovery. Medical suppression does not erase usage history.

Cooldown reductions help set the recovery period when you engage, but subsequent refunds cannot erase the hardware recovery floor. Cancelling, changing dimensions, dying or reconnecting does not reset that recovery. Consecutive-use pressure gradually decays while you rest.
Act between your enemies' reactions. Speed, perception and neurological consequences.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.service.inte: This implant can still gain internal upgrade levels even without a higher model in the catalog.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.service.no_s: Routine repair and +1 upgrades require the implant and service materials, but no fabrication schematic.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.service.pres: Both operations keep the same implant, its name, upgrades and installed data. Fill materials transfers only the required amounts; an explicit action creates the completed item.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.service.repa: This server has not defined repair materials for this implant.
Repair Station example: half integrity becomes 75% after one cycle. Existing upgrades are preserved.
Repair plan appears only when the item is damaged.

wiki.cyberneticenhancements.service.sepa: Repair restores integrity in 25% steps at a [[station_tech|Repair Station]]. Upgrade +1 improves performance at an [[station_upgrade|Upgrade Station]] without repairing wear.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.service.stag: No exposed stat delta on this level.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.service.upgr: This server has no +1 upgrade track for this implant.
Upgrade Station: next +1 level, same model and unchanged integrity.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.skills.dialo: Fixers and ripperdocs offer extra answers when a skill is high enough. Locked answers show the rank they need.
A passed check opens an extra line and a little commerce trust, within the daily limit. It never blocks a contract, and there are no dice rolls.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.skills.group: How well your body takes chrome, and what ripperdocs charge you.
How contacts treat you: prices, pay and trust.
Health, falls, healing and the damage the city deals.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.skills.notes: Every price, cost or loss reduction is held at no more than half of the base value, so nothing ever becomes free.
Servers can lower the rank limit, turn resetting off, or turn skills off entirely. Skills that are off keep their saved ranks and every dialogue check passes.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.skills.overv: Skills are passive talents. You never activate them: every rank you buy quietly improves something you already do, from the price of a purchase to how far you can fall.
There are 15 skills in four groups. Buy and review them in the Skills tab of the Neural Archive, where every skill shows its current bonus and what the next rank adds.
Each skill has ranks from 0 to %s. A rank gives a tenth of the skill's top bonus, so every single rank is felt.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.skills.per_r: Each rank gives a tenth of the top bonus.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.skills.point: Every [[system_street_cred|Street Cred]] level gives one skill point, and level 1 already gives one. A rank costs one point. Only the ranks you bought are stored, so your points can never drift away from your Street Cred.
There is no way to take a single point back. Reset skills in the Skills tab returns every bought rank at once, after a confirmation.
A reset costs %s eddies for every rank you had bought. Permanent lifepath ranks are kept.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.skills.subti: Passive talents that grow with your name.

wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.drop: Open the Quests tab and press Get Dropoff Point & Close to receive one free barrel and return to the world. Place it to register it and unlock that tab. If you lose the starter barrel, craft a replacement from a barrel, paper and an iron ingot. Your most recently placed or opened Dropoff Point receives future deliveries. Other players cannot open or register your barrel.

Turn in ready contracts from the Quests tab or over a call. Required quest items are taken from your inventory, while money, trust and XP are awarded immediately. Item rewards, including bonus schematics, arrive in your Dropoff Point within one Minecraft day. Turn in directly at the NPC to receive item rewards immediately instead.

The barrel has 27 slots. New quest deliveries show a cyan holographic ! above your barrel until you check it. A local arrival chat message can be toggled in Client config. If it is missing, full or in an unloaded chunk, undelivered items remain saved until a registered barrel can accept them. Placing or opening another barrel you own changes your delivery destination. Pending deliveries survive death, logout and server restarts.
Your personal barrel for remote quest reward deliveries.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.fabr: The Schematics tab shows owned and missing designs. Missing designs use black silhouettes and encrypted names; their details cannot be opened. Learned designs show recipes and the original discovery history.

Choose a learned or public design, inspect its layout, then use Fill grid and Fabricate. Fabrication repeats until ingredients run short or the output is full. Ingredients are consumed when each assembly completes. Stop leaves unfinished ingredients intact; Clear grid returns them. For automation, select a design, feed matching ingredients from above or the sides, and collect output from below. Each rising redstone edge starts exactly one craft. The signal may turn off while it runs. Pulses while busy or unable to craft are ignored, never queued; a held signal does not repeat. Configured schematic authorization survives reloads and does not require the player to stay online.
A full output bay pauses assembly. No fuel, redstone power or external energy supply is required.

Right-click a schematic to learn it, consuming one item and gaining 10 XP points on first discovery. Already-learned schematics are not consumed. In the Neural Archive, you can pay to extract a learned design back into a schematic item. Relearning it gives no additional XP. Unknown designs appear in the Fabricator as black silhouettes with encrypted names, and remain uncraftable until learned. Their recipe details stay hidden from JEI and wiki layouts. Use the pin icon to keep a design at the top of the list.
Manufacture implants, chipware, modules and workshop components in a 5x5 assembly grid.
Every Fabricator supports tiers 1-5 by default. Recipes still require their materials and any associated schematic.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.recy: Recycle cyberware into up to three function-specific material types. Good, worn and heavily damaged implants have distinct, deterministic recovery bands.
Recycle limb modules into micro actuators.
Recycle consumables into wiring, paste or circuit plates by category.

The Recycler previews recovery from server recipes. Press Recycle to start a three-second cycle per input. It repeats until input empties or the 5 by 5 recovery grid fills. Stop cancels an unfinished cycle without consuming input.

Items and progress stay in the station when its screen closes. Hoppers and pipes insert from above or the sides and extract recovery from below. Each rising redstone edge recycles exactly one input. The signal may turn off while it runs. Pulses while busy or unable to recycle are ignored, never queued; a held signal does not repeat.
Break down cyberware, modules, chipware and consumables into reusable parts.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.reli: This is a simplified example of overlapping sequences, not a complete high-tier puzzle. Start at top-row step 1 for 55.
Your second pick must stay in the same column, so move down to step 2 for BD, then across that row to step 3 for 4C.
At that point Daemon 1 is already cleared, because 55 BD 4C now appears in your path.
From step 3, move down the same column to FF, then across the last row to 0A. Those last two picks clear Daemon 2 as BD 4C FF and Daemon 3 as 4C FF 0A.
Daemon Chain
Example Route
Select tokens from the highlighted top row first, then alternate between the matching column and matching row.
A daemon is cleared once its full token sequence appears anywhere in the path you have built.
Clear every daemon before time or buffer runs out. Buffers hold 7/8/8/9 picks for Uncommon/Rare/Epic/Legendary caches. Higher tiers require longer overlapping sequences.
Daemons do not grant separate effects or partial rewards. The cache opens only when every listed daemon is cleared.
Start by scanning the daemon sequences on the right and look for shared middle or ending tokens.
Because the path only has to contain the sequence, you can route one daemon into another instead of solving each one separately.
Selected cells are numbered on the grid, so you can review the full route directly while planning the next pick.
Hovered cells show whether the current line is legal. If a token is off the active row or column, it cannot be picked yet.
You can close the screen to deal with combat or reposition, then reopen the same cache and continue the same run if time remains.
Each placed Relic Cache keeps its own matrix and daemon list until that cache is opened.
Plan before selecting: the first pick starts the breach timer. Uncommon/Rare/Epic/Legendary caches allow 50/40/32/25 seconds. Closing an executing breach does not pause it.

Caches can award intact equipment, service materials, schematic discoveries and specialized fabrication parts. Item rewards depend on the server loot tables. Successfully breaching an Uncommon/Rare/Epic/Legendary cache also awards 20/35/55/80 XP points once per player and cache. Failed attempts give no XP. Survival caches cannot be collected and relocated for repeated rewards; claim history survives death.
Uncommon caches replace one chest or barrel in igloo basements, jungle temples and pillager outposts.
Rare caches replace one chest or barrel in desert pyramids, woodland mansions and strongholds.
Epic caches replace one chest or barrel in trial chambers, ancient cities and bastion remnants.
Legendary caches replace one chest or barrel in end cities.
Bundled loot includes one primary reward, one or two support rolls and one fabrication-discovery roll. Server datapacks can change these pools.

Placement also checks older loaded structures, but only untouched loot-table chests or barrels. Opened containers, player storage and double chests are preserved. Each supported structure receives at most one generated cache.

Ask a [[npc_fixer|Fixer]] or [[npc_netrunner|Netrunner]] about nearby relic caches to mark the nearest known cache you have not breached on your HUD compass. No compass item is required. They do not reveal unexplored terrain. The Relic Scanner highlights every cache tier and prioritizes caches over ordinary containers within scan range.
Tiered breach caches placed into high-value structures.
Relic Caches
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.ripp: Inspect passive effects, active implants, upgrade level and integrity.
Manage chipware and modules when the selected implant supports them.
Open the archive directly from the station UI.
The Ripper Station is the main body-management screen.
It exposes body slots, current installed hardware, chrome totals and slot-by-slot planning.
Install, compare and manage cyberware, chipware and modules.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.tech: A Neural Fault makes the integrity bar fully red until cleared. Otherwise, the bar shows current integrity and a faint preview of the next 25% repair. Each cycle costs one quarter of the configured repair materials, rounded up to at least one item of each type.
All implant tiers are supported from the start. No machine or personal service capacity upgrades are required.

Repairs preserve installed chips, modules, upgrade levels and custom names. Neural Faults disable an implant and its attached chips or modules until a Repair Station clears the fault. [[cyberpsychosis|Cyberpsychosis]] has a 35% chance to leave one fault; with at least three implants, 20% of those events affect a second implant. Each loses 35-60% of maximum integrity. Normal gameplay wear is one quarter of its previous rate.
The Repair Station restores existing implants. Upgrade levels are applied at the separate [[station_upgrade|Upgrade Station]].

The Repair Station shares the [[station_upgrade|Upgrade Station]] layout and controls. Each four-second repair restores 25% of maximum integrity to the same implant. Normally, repair requires at least 25% missing integrity. With a Neural Fault, the first cycle only clears the fault and leaves integrity unchanged. Subsequent cycles repair integrity normally.

Place materials manually, shift-click them or use Fill materials; Creative fills are free. Stop cancels unfinished work without consuming inputs. Inventory and progress remain in the station after closing or saving. Hoppers and pipes feed implants and materials from above or the sides and retrieve completed items below. Each rising redstone edge starts one repair; busy or invalid pulses are ignored without queuing.
Restore damaged cyberware while retaining upgrades and custom data.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.upgr: Repair, Upgrade and Recycler stations support all implant tiers by default. No service capacity upgrades are required.
Upgrading preserves current integrity, name, installed chips, modules and other item data. It never grants a repair.
Each step uses its server datapack price and adds exactly one level. The item page shows the current track, level cap and numerical benefits.
The Upgrade Station never changes the model or manufactured tier. Model conversions use an explicit [[station_fabricator|Fabricator]] recipe and its schematic requirements.

Insert an uninstalled implant, supply up to two materials, and press Upgrade. A four-second cycle adds exactly one level to that same implant in place. Stop cancels unfinished work without consuming inputs. Hover the implant to inspect the next upgrade benefits. In Creative, Fill materials supplies the requirements for free. Inventory and progress stay in the station when closed. Hoppers and pipes insert implants and materials from above or the sides and retrieve the implant from below after an upgrade completes. Each rising redstone edge starts one upgrade; busy or invalid pulses are ignored and never queued.
Improve the same physical implant through its server-defined +1 track.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.status.bleed: Damage taken per stack during active aggression: +%s
This status is meant to read as active bleeding under exertion.
Moving while bleeding increases the periodic damage.
Periodic behavior: bleed damage over time.

wiki.cyberneticenhancements.status.corro: This status is meant to read as chemical breakdown.
Periodic behavior: steady corrosion damage over time.
Visual identity: toxic yellow-green dust, runoff and corrosive drip lines.
This status is meant to read as a deliberate tracking lock, not an enchantment reuse.
Periodic behavior: target outline highlighting for follow-up attacks.
Visual identity: cyan-green targeting rings plus the shared outline renderer.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.status.overh: This status is meant to read as internal thermal overload.
Moving while overheated increases the periodic damage.
Periodic behavior: keeps the target burning and deals fire-style damage pulses.
Visual identity: flame, ember dust, smoke plumes and heat rings.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.status.shock: This status is meant to read as electrical seizure, not a generic potion effect.
Periodic behavior: electrical jitter, movement disruption and outline highlighting.
Visual identity: cyan-white sparks, electric dust and violent body jitter.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.status.traum: This status is meant to read as blunt internal damage.
Periodic behavior: dampens movement and makes displacement worse.
Visual identity: red impact dust, damage bursts and heavy shock pulses.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.streetcred.d: Whenever your Street Cred changes, a small panel opens in the same place as calls and contracts. It shows the change, your level and rank, and how far you are from the next level.
The panel appears even when other HUD parts are hidden. If a call or the contact list is open, it waits until they close. A level-up stays on screen longer, and a new rank is named.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.streetcred.e: Hacking open a relic cache for the first time: %s to %s points, more for the rarer caches.
Discovering a large chromium deposit: %s points.
Finishing a contract: %s to %s points, more for harder contract types and higher tiers. Contracts are the steady way up.
Putting down a cyberpsycho: %s to %s points, more for the higher tiers. It counts whether or not a contract asked for it.
Street Cred is earned by doing the work of the city and coming out of it alive. Each of these pays once for each thing you do:
Defeating a full MaxTac squad that was sent after you: %s points.
Nothing pays for time spent, and nothing can be repeated: a cache, a card, a schematic or a deposit only counts the first time. Street Cred is never lost, not even by dying.
A name only ever helps. Every bonus grows evenly with each level, from nothing at level 1 to its maximum at the top, so every level is felt a little.
Nothing is ever taken away: a low name simply gets none of this. Every level also gives one skill point to spend on [[skills_overview|Skills]].
Contract pay: up to +%s%% on the money of every contract, on top of any lifepath bonus.
Prices: up to %s%% off at every contact that sells, stacking with trust discounts and the lifepath.
Dangerous work: from level %s issuers offer tier 2 contracts and from level %s tier 3, even before they trust you enough on their own.
Trust: contacts warm to you up to %s%% faster, so discounts and better work arrive sooner.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.streetcred.o: Street Cred is a measure of how well known you are in the city. It is a single level from 1 to %s that only ever goes up, and it is never lost.
Everyone starts at level 1 as a nobody. As your Street Cred grows, your level and the rank that goes with it grow too.
Street Cred is yours alone. It stays with you through death, and other players cannot raise or lower it.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.streetcred.p: Street Cred is counted in points. The first level costs %s points and every level after it costs %s more than the one before. Reaching level %s takes %s points in total.
A [[origin_street_kid|Street Kid]] earns %s%% more Street Cred from everything, because the street remembers its own. The other lifepaths earn it at the normal rate.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.streetcred.s: How well the city knows your name.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.system.cyber: Cyberstrain has no passive stat penalties. At or above the psychosis-risk threshold, accumulated instability can trigger an [[cyberpsychosis|episode]].
Suppression medicine temporarily reduces effective cyberstrain.
Frontal cortex hardware can add extra cyberstrain on top of installed chrome.
Use lower-cost implants for early builds.
Use suppressants when pushing into high-strain setups.
Treat active cyberware and stimulant use as part of the risk budget, not just the installed load.
The pressure system that limits how much chrome a body can run safely.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.system.progr: Cyberware, chipware, limb modules and advanced parts are manufactured in the [[station_fabricator|Fabricator]]. Basic supplies, consumables and machine blocks also use crafting-table recipes.
Public designs are available immediately. Schematic-locked recipes remain hidden and unusable until learned, including in JEI and the Fabricator.
[[station_fabricator|Fabricator]], [[station_tech|Repair]], [[station_upgrade|Upgrade]] and [[station_recycler|Recycler]] stations support every implant tier from the start.
[[station_relic_cache|Relic Cache]] world generation is live. Each supported structure replaces one chest or barrel with a tiered cache block.
Uncommon: igloo basement, jungle temple, pillager outpost. Rare: desert pyramid, woodland mansion, stronghold.
Epic: trial chambers, ancient city, bastion remnant. Legendary: end city.

[[npc_techie|Techies]], [[npc_netrunner|Netrunners]] and [[npc_merc|Mercs]] issue seven kinds of contracts, including dangerous Cyberpsycho Sightings with the highest money payouts. Dialogue and the [[quest_guide_overview|quest archive]] track the current objective and return to the issuer.

Rewards include eurodollars, trust and supplies, with a chance for schematic or part discoveries. With bundled settings, ordinary contracts reach tier-four designs; tier-three Cyberpsycho Sightings can also award tier-five designs and restricted cores.
Item pages use current server recipes and service definitions. Cache loot is controlled by server tables; the cache preview is a sample of possible rewards, not a promise of drops.
A model conversion is a Fabricator recipe. A +1 improvement preserves the same model; repairs restore integrity and clear Neural Faults. Players have 100 base Chrome capacity.
The live acquisition split and implemented world sources.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.system.psych: Immunoblockers and Chrome Suppressant reduce instability and can shorten an active episode.
After an episode ends, Aftershock remains briefly and keeps some penalties active.
High-strain crisis behavior driven by effective cyberstrain plus instability.
Episodes prioritize reachable players, NPCs, pets, hostile mobs, then passive mobs. Stalled targets are temporarily skipped.
Ignored targets include configured nuisance types such as bats, fish, silverfish and endermites.
Minor episode: temporary combat bonuses and involuntary pursuit, preceded by an onset animation.
Major episode: stronger combat bonuses and involuntary pursuit. Both episode types end with an exhausted recovery animation.
Cyberpsychosis does not trigger from installed chrome alone. It requires psychosis-risk [[cyberstrain|cyberstrain]] plus accumulated instability.
Instability builds from combat, cyberware activations, certain consumables and remaining at or above the psychosis-risk threshold.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.world_encoun: A holographic panel hangs in the doorway of the vehicle to mark it as restricted. It is only light: you can walk straight through it, so it is a warning and not a lock.
Yellow with a ! means the site is open to you. You have done nothing to the crew or their cache, and the leader still deals with you. Treat it as a reminder that everything inside belongs to MedTec.

Red with an X means you have wronged the site: you opened its chest or relic cache, broke part of the build, or struck one of the crew. The leader refuses to offer you the quest again, for good, and the barrier shows this to you alone. If you walk through the barrier anyway, the crew attacks on sight. Other players still see their own colour.

Red with a countdown means you failed the Missing Patient quest. The leader will not deal with you for fifteen minutes, and the barrier counts down the time left. When it runs out, the barrier fades back to yellow with a soft chime and the leader will offer the quest again. Walking through it in the meantime still makes the crew attack.
Badlands
Forests
Biomes
Biomes from other mods that join the vanilla forest, taiga, savanna or badlands groups can host it too.
The site can generate in any of the Overworld biomes below. Look for flat, open ground away from dense settlements.

A MedTec recovery vehicle parked out in the wild, with a small crew standing guard around it. The site is company property and the crew behaves accordingly.
World encounters are places you stumble on while exploring, unlike street encounters, which find you.

Three MedTec staff stand guard. The leader waits inside by the door, and two bystanders with grey names, who will not talk, stand outside on either side of the entrance stairs. They never wander off, but they turn to watch you. A fourth sits on the bench inside the vehicle, next to its loot. Opening the chest or breaking into a relic cache there turns all of them against you.
The leader sells nothing and offers no services. They explain the situation and hand out the one quest, which opens as soon as you speak to them.
Missing Patient: a MedTec patient has gone missing and the tracking system is down. The coordinates are only roughly right, so you must search the marked area on your compass.
The patient lies somewhere inside the area, never at its centre, and only appears once you are within about 110 blocks. They glow when you get close. Walk right up to them to find them.
Nothing needs to be carried back. Return to the leader and tell them in person to be paid.

About a third of all containers hide sealed cargo in one of their crates. That crate has a golden "!" floating over it and nothing above it, so it can be spotted from across the container. Taking the cargo counts as finding it.
Crates

Crates stand in groups with gaps between, up to three high. Each holds one to four kinds of its container's cargo, and the number of slots fits what is inside. Items can be taken out but not put in, and a crate breaks at once.

Unassembled cyberware parts: common to epic item components, chromium alloy and scrap, joints, servo screws, lenses, batteries, circuit plates and wiring. The best grades are rare.

Freight containers that went over the side of a ship and ended up in the shallows. They lie on beaches, on the sea floor and among coral reefs, some whole, some snapped in half or torn open, some toppled onto their side, and all stacked with wooden crates of cargo.
Nobody guards them. A container is a place to search: every one carries a single kind of cargo, and some hide sealed cargo that belongs to one of your contacts.

Found cargo: when you pick up sealed cargo it is matched to one of your permanent contacts, and a Salvage contract opens at once. Bring the cargo to that contact in person to be paid and earn their trust.

Lost shipment: a contact can instead ask you to retrieve cargo that went down with a container. They point you to the nearest one, and the cargo waits in a crate marked with a golden "!" inside it. Bring it back in person.
Either way, everything else in the container is yours to keep. If the cargo goes missing again, nobody blames you: there is no penalty, the contract simply ends.

Shipping Containers
Swim along the coast or dive in the open ocean. Containers settle on flat sand, gravel or the sea floor, and are rare enough that you may have to cover a lot of shoreline.
Locate them with the locate command and the shipping container structure, or ask a contact about a lost shipment, which sends you to the nearest one.
